Definition: from G1223 and G2476; to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove, intervene:--go further, be parted, after the space of.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to stand apart, to step away or be parted from someone. Luke uses it when Jesus is parted from His disciples at the ascension, and when the ship's crew had gone a little further before sounding again. It also marks the space of about an hour between Peter's denials.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe parting is part of the story, not the end of it. Jesus was parted from His disciples only to be enthroned, and the distance never broke the promise that He would be with them.
